A History in Four Documents.name: A History in Four Documents
A History in Four Documents.description: Four documents. One nation. Join Founding Father Roger Sherman as he traces the remarkable story of American liberty through history's most transformative texts.

American Closing Cermemony.name: American Closing Cermemony
American Closing Cermemony.description: The stars and stripes take center stage as the American Army brings the festival to a triumphant and patriotic close.

Break Bread with the Brits.name: Break Bread with the Brits
Break Bread with the Brits.description: Taste a traditional colonial drink, breads and jellies while you discuss happenings in the rebellious colonies with those loyal to the crown.
Break Bread with the Brits.additionalText: Must be 16 or older.  Donations Strongly Encouraged

British Children's Militia.name: British Children's Militia
British Children's Militia.description: The Crown's youngest soldiers are ready for inspection — cheer on the British Children's Militia as they drill with pride and precision.

British Daily Retreat.name: British Daily Retreat
British Daily Retreat.description: The King's forces end their duty day and retire the Colour.

British Muster & Drill.name: British Muster & Drill
British Muster & Drill.description: The King's forces maneuver and drill, preparing to suppress the rebellion.

British Swordplay.name: British Swordplay
British Swordplay.description: Watch British military demonstrate offensive and defensive techniques.

Broom Making Demonstration.name: Broom Making Demonstration
Broom Making Demonstration.description: It's older than the Revolution and harder than it looks. Watch a skilled artisan craft a broom using the same techniques colonial Americans relied on daily.

Calligraphy I.name: Calligraphy I
Calligraphy I.description: Beginners use pencil to learn the basic strokes that form 18th century script.

Calligraphy II.name: Calligraphy II
Calligraphy II.description: Quill and ink instruction appropriate for adults and mature youth ($5 fee)

Children's Militia.name: Children's Militia
Children's Militia.description: Young colonists muster & march to show their patriotism.

Colonial Dance.name: Colonial Dance
Colonial Dance.description: Join a colonial dance for adults and children old enough to follow instruction and participate in dancing.

Colonial Dance Instruction.name: Colonial Dance Instruction
Colonial Dance Instruction.description: Join this favorite pastime and learn some favorite colonial dances.

Colonial Economics and the Secret Commit.name: Colonial Economics and the Secret Committee
Colonial Economics and the Secret Commit.description: Behind the battles was a shadow economy. Uncover the covert trade networks and financial schemes that kept the American Revolution alive.

Colonial Folk Songs.name: Colonial Folk Songs
Colonial Folk Songs.description: Enjoy some of the lesser-known songs of the American colonial era.

Colonial School.name: Colonial School
Colonial School.description: Children attend school for academic, etiquette, and moral lessons of the day.

Continental Artillery.name: Continental Artillery
Continental Artillery.description: Feel the ground shake as Continental artillery roars to life — a thunderous demonstration of the firepower that turned the tide of revolution.

Continental Muster and Drill.name: Continental Muster and Drill
Continental Muster and Drill.description: Watch Continental soldiers and militia unite to drill and fire muskets in a thrilling demonstration of the military force that won American independence.

Declaration of Independence I.name: Declaration of Independence I
Declaration of Independence I.description: Hear the Declaration of Independence as read by Founding Fathers and others affected by its ideas. Ask a founder a question.

Declaration of Independence II.name: Declaration of Independence II
Declaration of Independence II.description: Hear the Declaration of Independence as read by Founding Fathers and others affected by its ideas. Ask a founder a question.

Dressing a Lady.name: Dressing a Lady
Dressing a Lady.description: From stays to silk — join Lady Dunmore as she dresses for the day and uncovers the elaborate world of colonial fashion, layer by layer.

people.character: Lady Charlotte Stewart Murray, Countess of Dunmore

Dressing an 18th Century Couple.name: Dressing an 18th Century Couple
Dressing an 18th Century Couple.description: A review of the layers of clothing that a working-class colonial couple would wear.

Drop Spindle Class.name: Drop Spindle Class
Drop Spindle Class.description: Before spinning wheels, there was the drop spindle. Try your hand at this essential colonial skill and leave with yarn you made yourself.

Early Printings of the Declaration of In.name: Early Printings of the Declaration of Independence
Early Printings of the Declaration of In.description: The ink was barely dry before it changed the world. Discover the fascinating story behind the early printings of the Declaration of Independence.

Elevenses.name: Elevenses
Elevenses.description: Taste a traditional colonial drink, biscuits and tarts while you sit and visit with the founders about the ideas of the revolution.
Elevenses.additionalText: Must be 16 or older.  Donations Strongly Encouraged

Elevenses continued.name: Elevenses continued

Fan Painting Class.name: Fan Painting Class
Fan Painting Class.description: Fans weren't just for cooling off — they were colonial art. Join this charming class and paint your own piece of 18th-century elegance to take home.

Finding Noon by The Sun.name: Finding Noon by The Sun
Finding Noon by The Sun.description: Discover how 18th-century Americans told time using the sun — a hands-on demonstration of the clever science behind colonial timekeeping.

French Expeditionary Corps.name: French Expeditionary Corps
French Expeditionary Corps.description: 6,000 French soldiers. One crucial alliance. Learn how Rochambeau's corps helped deliver the decisive blow at Yorktown.

From the Stamp Act to Independence.name: From the Stamp Act to Independence
From the Stamp Act to Independence.description: It began with a stamp and ended with a revolution. Follow the remarkable chain of events that transformed loyal British subjects into American patriots.

God and Gunpowder: the Revolutionary Cle.name: God and Gunpowder: the Revolutionary Clergy
God and Gunpowder: the Revolutionary Cle.description: Musket in one hand, Bible in the other — discover the firebrand preachers whose sermons helped ignite and sustain the American Revolution.

Hammered Dulcimer.name: Hammered Dulcimer
Hammered Dulcimer.description: Listen to a performance of this classical 18th century instrument.

Hog Thief Trial.name: Hog Thief Trial
Hog Thief Trial.description: Someone stole the hog — but who? Take your seat on the jury, hear the evidence, and deliver your verdict in this rowdy colonial courtroom!

Introduction to Natural Law.name: Introduction to Natural Law
Introduction to Natural Law.description: Before the Revolution came an idea. Discover the philosophy of Natural Law — the intellectual spark that convinced the founders they had every right to rebel.

Learn about Henry Knox.name: Learn about Henry Knox
Learn about Henry Knox.description: From Boston bookshop to battlefield hero — discover how Henry Knox taught himself artillery from books and became Washington's most indispensable general

Liberty or Death: You Decide Virginia's.name: Liberty or Death: You Decide Virginia's Fate
Liberty or Death: You Decide Virginia's.description: Patrick Henry demands liberty or death. Washington and Jefferson weigh the consequences. As a Virginia delegate, YOUR vote will determine the colony's fate.

Life of a Laundress: A Demonstration of.name: Life of a Laundress: A Demonstration of 18th Century Laundry
Life of a Laundress: A Demonstration of.description: Clean clothes in colonial America came at a price — hours of back-breaking labor. Watch a live demonstration of the skills that kept the Revolution looking sharp.

Lord and Lady Dunmore's Parlor.name: Lord and Lady Dunmore's Parlor
Lord and Lady Dunmore's Parlor.description: Behind the politics and controversy, a family called Virginia home. Share a parlor visit with Lord and Lady Dunmore in their elegant world.

Lucet Class.name: Lucet Class
Lucet Class.description: Learn to work this ancient tool to make cord for laces, draw-strings, etc.

Madison debates Henry.name: Madison debates Henry
Madison debates Henry.description: He wrote the Constitution. Patrick Henry hated it. Watch James Madison defend his masterpiece against Virginia's most passionate and fiery orator.

Meet Benjamin Franklin.name: Meet Benjamin Franklin
Meet Benjamin Franklin.description: He flew a kite in a thunderstorm and negotiated with kings. Meet Benjamin Franklin — America's most irresistible genius and the Revolution's secret weapon.

Meet Billy Lee.name: Meet Billy Lee
Meet Billy Lee.description: No one knew George Washington more intimately than Billy Lee. Meet the enslaved man who served at the General's side from Boston to Yorktown.

Meet Christopher Gadsden.name: Meet Christopher Gadsden
Meet Christopher Gadsden.description: He was called the Sam Adams of the South. Meet Christopher Gadsden — merchant, soldier, and one of the Revolution's most passionate and uncompromising voices.

Meet Elizabeth Burgin.name: Meet Elizabeth Burgin
Meet Elizabeth Burgin.description: She rescued over 200 American prisoners from British ships and became one of the Revolution's most wanted women. Meet the remarkable Elizabeth Burgin.

Meet Elizabeth Powell.name: Meet Elizabeth Powell
Meet Elizabeth Powell.description: She dined with Washington, debated with Franklin, and influenced the founders more than history remembers. Meet Philadelphia's most brilliant and powerful woman, Elizabeth Powel.

Meet General O'Hara.name: Meet General O'Hara
Meet General O'Hara.description: He handed over the sword at Yorktown. Meet General O'Hara, the British officer who stood at the Revolution's final, defining moment.

Meet George Mason.name: Meet George Mason
Meet George Mason.description: He wrote the words that inspired the Bill of Rights and pushed Virginia to curtail slavery. Meet the complex, principled patriot George Mason.

Meet George Washington.name: Meet George Washington
Meet George Washington.description: He led a ragged army to victory against the world's greatest military power. Come face to face with General George Washington himself.

Meet Governor Dunmore.name: Meet Governor Dunmore
Meet Governor Dunmore.description: He promised freedom to enslaved Americans — then used it as a weapon against the Revolution. Meet Lord Dunmore, the royal governor who lit a powder keg.

Meet Governor Galvez.name: Meet Governor Galvez
Meet Governor Galvez.description: He fought the British while America fought for independence. Meet Bernardo de Galvez — the Spanish hero the history books forgot.

Meet Haym Salomon.name: Meet Haym Salomon
Meet Haym Salomon.description: George Washington was desperate for money. Haym Salomon had the answer. Meet the remarkable patriot who quietly saved the American Revolution.

Meet James Madison.name: Meet James Madison
Meet James Madison.description: A conversation with the Father of the United States Constitution.

Meet John Adams.name: Meet John Adams
Meet John Adams.description: A conversation with the titan of American Independence.

Meet John Dickinson.name: Meet John Dickinson
Meet John Dickinson.description: Discover the "Penman of the Revolution" — the Founding Father whose powerful words shaped American liberty before anyone fired a shot.

Meet John Hancock.name: Meet John Hancock
Meet John Hancock.description: A conversation with the man who lead the Continental Congress to independence.

Meet Lydia Darragh.name: Meet Lydia Darragh
Meet Lydia Darragh.description: She was a quiet Quaker mother who became one of Washington's most valuable spies. Discover the remarkable true story of patriot hero Lydia Darragh.

Meet Major James Beaumont.name: Meet Major James Beaumont
Meet Major James Beaumont.description: Proper, proud, and loyal to the Crown — meet Major James Beaumont, the British officer who sees this colonial rebellion as a temporary inconvenience.

Meet Mercy Otis Warren.name: Meet Mercy Otis Warren
Meet Mercy Otis Warren.description: Poet, playwright, spy-master, and historian — meet Mercy Otis Warren, the razor-sharp patriot whose pen was as powerful as any musket.

Meet Lt. Alexander Chesney.name: Meet Lt. Alexander Chesney
Meet Lt. Alexander Chesney.description: Join Lt. Chesney of South Carolina to hear his adventures with the Militia. Will you enlist to serve under the war's top marksman?

Meet Patrick Henry.name: Meet Patrick Henry
Meet Patrick Henry.description: A conversation with one of the revolution's top orators.

Meet Peter Muhlenberg.name: Meet Peter Muhlenberg
Meet Peter Muhlenberg.description: There is a time for prayer and a time for war. Meet Peter Muhlenberg — the fighting parson who chose both and changed history.

Meet Robert Shurliff.name: Meet Robert Shurliff
Meet Robert Shurliff.description: Robert Shurtliff served bravely in the Continental Army — but harbored an extraordinary secret. Meet the soldier whose true identity would shock the founding era.

Meet Ruth Harrington.name: Meet Ruth Harrington
Meet Ruth Harrington.description: She watched the Revolution begin at her own doorstep. Meet Ruth Harrington, who paid a devastating price on April 19, 1775

Meet Sybil Ludington.name: Meet Sybil Ludington
Meet Sybil Ludington.description: You've heard of Paul Revere's ride; now listen to Sybil tell of her harrowing ride.

Minuet Dance Demonstration.name: Minuet Dance Demonstration
Minuet Dance Demonstration.description: Discover how the founders danced — a captivating demonstration of the minuet, the fashionable step that graced every colonial ballroom.

Morning Toilette.name: Morning Toilette
Morning Toilette.description: Getting dressed in the 18th century was no simple task. Experience the fascinating morning routines that defined style, status, and society in colonial America.

Never Caught.name: Never Caught
Never Caught.description: Hear the adventures of Ona Judge, escaped from servitude at Mt. Vernon.

Piracy Trial.name: Piracy Trial
Piracy Trial.description: In this Admiralty Court, will we hang another pirate or convict a smuggler?

Redress or Revolution: You Decide the Fa.name: Redress or Revolution: You Decide the Fate of the Colonies
Redress or Revolution: You Decide the Fa.description: It's 1775 and the colonies are at a crossroads. Take your seat in Congress, hear the debate, and cast the vote that decides America's fate.

Reveille with the King's Forces.name: Reveille with the King's Forces
Reveille with the King's Forces.description: The King's forces begin their duty day with morning assembly, roll call, and posting the Colour.

Revolution from the \"Billy\" point of v.name: Revolution from the "Billy" point of view
Revolution from the \"Billy\" point of v.description: One served beside Washington in bondage. One fought beside him as a free man. Hear Billy Lee and Billy Flora tell the stories history almost forgot.

Setup / Takedown.description: Time reserved for setting up or cleaning up

Shut-the-Box.name: Shut-the-Box
Shut-the-Box.description: Enter a tournament playing a popular game of chance and skill for a prize.

Sipping Chocolate and Spilling Tea.name: Sipping Chocolate and Spilling Tea
Sipping Chocolate and Spilling Tea.description: Sip chocolate with Lady Dunmore and weigh in — should Virginia stand with Boston under the Intolerable Acts, or stay loyal to the Crown?  Sorry, gents, this is a ladies-only event.

The Dark times of 1776.name: The Dark times of 1776
The Dark times of 1776.description: In 1776, the Revolution nearly died. Meet John Glover — the Marblehead mariner whose men pulled Washington back from the brink of total defeat.

The language of the Fan.name: The language of the Fan
The language of the Fan.description: In colonial society, a fan spoke volumes. Uncover the hidden messages behind every fold and gesture of this elegant secret language.

The powder Incident.name: The powder Incident
The powder Incident.description: One day after Lexington and Concord, Virginia had its own powder keg moment. Discover how Governor Dunmore's midnight raid nearly ignited the Revolution.

The Wartime Role of an Officer's Wife.description: She didn't carry a musket, but she was indispensable. Explore the remarkable role officer's wives played in keeping the British Army together on campaign.

Benjamin Franklin.desc: Printer, scientist, diplomat, and wit &emdash; Franklin charmed France into the alliance that made American independence possible.

Bernardo de Galvez.desc: Spanish governor who defied an empire to aid the Revolution, capturing British forts across the Gulf and changing the war's outcome.

Billy Flora.desc: Free Black hero of the Battle of Great Bridge who held the bridge single-handedly so his comrades could escape the British.

Billy Lee.desc: George Washington's enslaved personal attendant, Billy Lee rode beside him in battle and served through eight years of war.

Christopher Gadsden.desc: South Carolina's most passionate patriot &emdash; Gadsden designed the "Don't Tread on Me" flag and demanded independence before almost anyone else.

Comte de Rochambeau.desc: French general who commanded 6,000 troops at Yorktown and treated Washington as an equal when others would not.

Elizabeth Powell.desc: Philadelphia's most brilliant hostess &emdash; she challenged Washington to stay in public life and may have changed American history.

Elizabeth Burgen.desc: New York patriot who risked everything to help more than 200 American prisoners escape the horrors of British prison ships.

Francis Hopkinson.desc: New Jersey's most versatile founder &emdash; artist, lawyer, musician, and poet whose genius touched every corner of the new nation.

Colonel Birch.desc: Meet the British officer who gave thousands of Black Loyalists their freedom papers &emdash; one of the Revolution's more surprising acts of honor.

George Washington.desc: General, president, farmer &emdash; Washington was the one figure every founder trusted, the indispensable man of American independence.

George Mason.desc: Virginia's brilliant, forgotten founder wrote the Declaration of Rights &emdash; and refused to sign the Constitution because it protected slavery.

Governor Dunmore.desc: Virginia's last royal governor tried to crush rebellion, burned Norfolk, and promised freedom to enslaved people who joined the British.

Hyam Soloman.desc: Polish-born Jewish financier Haym Salomon personally raised funds that kept the Continental Army in the field through its darkest hours.

Isaiah Thomas.desc: His printing press was a weapon. Isaiah Thomas spread the patriot cause across New England before the first shots were fired.

James Madison.desc: Small in stature, enormous in intellect &emdash; Madison designed the Constitution, defended it in the Federalist Papers, and shaped American government.

John Adams.desc: Stubborn, brilliant, and impossible to ignore &emdash; Adams argued America into independence and spent a lifetime defending what the founders built.

John Dickinson.desc: The "Penman of the Revolution" argued for reconciliation but served faithfully when independence came &emdash; a man of conscience and compromise.

John Glover.desc: Massachusetts fisherman whose Marblehead regiment ferried Washington's army across the Delaware &emdash; making the Trenton surprise possible.

John Hancock.desc: Boston's wealthiest merchant, president of the Continental Congress, and the man with the boldest signature on the Declaration of Independence.

John Paul Jones.desc: Scottish-born naval hero whose daring sea victories gave the fledgling American navy its first legends and its fighting motto.

Lydia Darragh.desc: Philadelphia Quaker who eavesdropped on British officers planning an attack, then risked her life to warn Washington in time.

Major Beaumont.desc: Through Major Beaumont's eyes, experience the Revolution from the other side &emdash; professional, principled, and far from home.

Mercy Otis Warren.desc: Massachusetts playwright and historian whose sharp pen mocked British tyranny &emdash; and whose history of the Revolution shaped American memory.

Ona Judge.desc: She risked everything for freedom and refused a comfortable return to captivity. Meet the woman who made the Washingtons face their own contradictions.

Lt. Alexander Chesney.desc: He chose the King over independence and paid dearly for it. Meet a loyalist officer whose story reveals the revolution's other half.

Patrick Henry.desc: Virginia's great orator &emdash; "Give me liberty or give me death!" &emdash; Henry's voice ignited a revolution and shaped the American conscience.

Peter Muhlenberg.desc: Lutheran pastor who shed his clerical robes mid-sermon to reveal a Continental uniform &emdash; then marched three hundred men to war.

Robert Morris.desc: The Revolution's banker &emdash; Morris used his personal fortune to keep Washington's army supplied when Congress could not or would not.

Robert Shurtliff.desc: He was a good soldier &emdash; until the army discovered "he" was a woman named Deborah Sampson who had fooled everyone for two years.

Roger Sherman.desc: Connecticut cobbler turned statesman &emdash; the only founder to sign all four of America's founding documents, from the Articles to the Constitution.

Ruth Harrington.desc: Her husband fell at Lexington. Ruth Harrington's story puts a human face on the morning the Revolutionary War began.

Samoset.desc: The Abenaki leader who walked into Plymouth Colony in 1621, greeted the Pilgrims in English, and made the first peace possible.

Sybil Ludington.desc: Paul Revere's ride was famous. Sybil Ludington's was twice as long &emdash; made by a sixteen-year-old girl on a rainy night.

Thomas Jefferson.desc: Architect of American ideals, Jefferson's words launched a nation. His contradictions &emdash; slaveholder and freedom's champion &emdash; still echo today.

Nathanael Greene.desc: He retreated brilliantly, conserved his army masterfully, and wore the British down until they had nothing left to fight with.

John Savage.desc: Meet Sergeant Savage: a British soldier trying to keep his men honorable while carrying out a war that tests every principle he holds.

Joseph Plumb Martin.desc: Connecticut private who left the most vivid memoir of the Revolution &emdash; cold, hungry, and faithful, he saw the war from the bottom up.

Colonel Desandrounis.desc: French military engineer who helped design the siege works at Yorktown &emdash; the technical genius whose fortifications made Cornwallis's surrender inevitable.

Count Von Fersen.desc: Swedish nobleman who served as aide to Rochambeau at Yorktown, fighting for American liberty on the other side of the world.

Marquis de Laval.desc: French nobleman who served with Rochambeau's forces, bringing aristocratic courage and European military skill to Yorktown's final campaign.

Penelope Barker.desc: Fifty-one women signed her proclamation. Barker's Edenton Tea Party proved colonial women had political opinions &emdash; and the courage to act.

Deborah Sampson.desc: Massachusetts woman who disguised herself as Robert Shurtliff, fought as a Continental soldier, and kept her secret through wounds and battle.

General O'Hara.desc: Meet the man who surrendered the British army at Yorktown &emdash; with one last diplomatic flourish that Washington quietly and firmly rejected.

Marie Clyne.desc: Camp follower, butter maker, lucet instructor
